source.headline: US Medium-Term Inflation Expectations Tick Down; Unemployment Expectations Deteriorate

learning_profile.reason: No directly matching ACTIONABLE v2 context segment was used to override current facts; relevant generic calibration was kept neutral.

predictions.mechanism: Slightly lower medium-term inflation expectations are marginally dovish, but the deterioration in unemployment expectations is growth-negative and current oil and Treasury-yield pressure offsets a clean risk-on read.
predictions.invalidation: A decisive move lower in Treasury yields and oil would tilt the signal bullish; a renewed jump in yields or energy would tilt it bearish.

predictions.mechanism: Lower three-year inflation expectations can support duration-sensitive growth stocks, but elevated long yields and oil-driven inflation risk prevent a clean upside call.
predictions.invalidation: A sustained drop in US10Y would favor upside; a break higher in US10Y with oil near or above $100 would favor downside.

predictions.mechanism: The deterioration in unemployment and job-finding expectations is mildly negative for more cyclical large-cap exposure, while the inflation signal is not dovish enough to fully offset it.
predictions.invalidation: A broad risk-on reversal led by falling yields and energy prices would neutralize the mild downside bias.
